title: SIP vs lump sum, and what to do when the market falls
publisher: Artha Kavach summary of public guidance (RBI / SEBI / IRDAI / Income Tax Dept) — pending manual verification
text: A lump sum puts all your money in at once; a SIP spreads it over months. Nobody can reliably time the market, so for regular monthly income a SIP is the natural fit, and if you have a big sum you can invest it in instalments over 6–12 months (an STP) to reduce regret. When markets fall, equity fund values drop on paper — this is normal and has happened many times. The costly mistake is panic-selling and stopping SIPs at the bottom; continuing a SIP during a fall buys more units cheaply. Check that your asset mix still matches your goal, keep your emergency fund separate so you are never forced to sell at a loss, and avoid checking your portfolio daily.
summary_hinglish: Lump sum mein ek saath invest, SIP mein mahino mein baant kar. Market timing koi nahi kar sakta. Market girne par panic mein sell karna aur SIP band karna sabse bada nuksan hai; girte market mein SIP chalane se zyada units sasta milte hain. Emergency fund alag rakho taki zabardasti na bechna pade.
summary_hi: लंपसम में एक साथ निवेश, SIP में महीनों में बांटकर। बाज़ार का समय कोई सही नहीं पकड़ सकता। गिरावट में घबराकर बेचना और SIP बंद करना सबसे बड़ी गलती है; गिरते बाज़ार में SIP चलाने से ज़्यादा यूनिट सस्ते मिलते हैं। आपातकालीन फंड अलग रखें।
